commodities.name: Corn
commodities.rationale: US Corn Belt summer heat (extreme degree-days above 29 °C, Schlenker & Roberts 2009) and rainfall around pollination/grain fill.

commodities.name: Soybeans
commodities.rationale: US July–August heat (>30 °C degree-days) and rainfall during pod set; Mato Grosso rainy-season rainfall (Nov–Feb).

commodities.name: Wheat (Chicago SRW)
commodities.rationale: Kansas spring rainfall and May–June heat during grain fill; Beauce (France) spring rainfall. Kansas is a hard-red-winter region, a proxy for the SRW contract.

commodities.name: Arabica coffee
commodities.rationale: Sul de Minas winter cold (frost risk, May–Sep) and rainfall during flowering/fruit set (Sep–Mar).

commodities.name: Natural gas (Henry Hub)
commodities.rationale: Heating + cooling degree-days (base 18 °C) at four US demand centres; NWP forecast level and week-on-week forecast revision (Mu 2007).

commodities.name: Cocoa
commodities.rationale: West African (Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana) 28-day rainfall anomaly, all year. Long tier only.

models.hm: Expanding historical mean of realised training returns (Campbell–Thompson benchmark).
models.mkt: Ridge on market features: 1-week return, 4-week return, 12-week realised volatility.
models.wx: Ridge on market features + weather features for the tier (nests mkt).

caveats: Continuous front-month (=F) Yahoo series contain roll jumps; weekly log returns are research proxies, not executable futures P&L.
Yahoo Finance chart endpoint is unofficial and may revise or omit sessions.
Weather points are equal-weighted representative coordinates, not production- or population-share weights.
ERA5 is reanalysis (modelled), lagged 7 days to respect publication latency; the ORACLE tier deliberately uses future realised weather and is an upper bound, not a forecast.
NWP tier uses Open-Meteo Previous Runs (from March 2024 only): ~2.7 years, so out-of-sample samples are small and crop features are active in only one or two seasons.
NWP anomalies are measured against ERA5 climatology without model-bias correction; the ridge intercept absorbs only a constant bias.
Many commodity × tier × horizon tests are run; Benjamini–Hochberg q-values are reported and should be used instead of raw p-values.
Sensitivity coefficients are full-sample, in-sample descriptive regressions, not forecasts.
No transaction costs, position sizing or trading rules are evaluated.
